title: Clocked Zero-Error Decision with Expected-Time Bound
statement: Let $S$ be a finite-state deterministic machine, $A$ a finite-state nondeterministic machine, $L$ a language of Boolean words, and $m,T_S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $S$ computes the all-true word of length $m(|x|)$ on every input $x$ within $T_S(|x|)$ steps, and $n\le m(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose every length-$m(|x|)$ witness on which an attempt by $A$ on $x$ halts with a single output bit yields the correct membership indicator, and that for every $x$ the probability that a uniformly random length-$m(|x|)$ witness does not yield such a bit is at most $3/4$. Then the clocked host machine built from $S$ and $A$ with its looping option enabled has cumulative nonhalting probability at most $T_S(n)+m(n)+2+16(m(n)+1)$: for every natural number $K$, the sum over $t<K$ of the probability that it has not halted after $t$ steps is at most this bound. Every witness on which it halts produces exactly the one-bit membership indicator of $L$.

$A$ is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine
